## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [27. November 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.66
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.66
- Datum: 27.11.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
c/o Editora Guanabara
132 rua Ouvidor
Rio de Janeiro. Rio, 27.11.40

Dear Hanna u Manfred,
We have not had any letters
from you last week and so far not
this week, and I am glad we had at
least the cable giving us your new
address. From us there is little to re-
port. We had a quiet week, did not
see many people, enjoyed our balcony
and the fact that it is not yet hot.
Our plans are still uncertain. We
intend to stay here in the Hotel Centra
as long as it does not get too hot,
and then - by the middle or end of
January - we would like to go to
Newyork during the hot season here.
But it is a very expensive journey,
and therefore it would be good if
you could enquire at the Pal. Lloyd
by phone perhaps about the possibility
of sending the ticket from Engl or to pay
it there and give instructions to book
here to make it out for us. Perhaps you
or the travel bureau could wire us
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Aerogramm-Formular. Die Tinte ist gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
whether this can be done without
difficulty and how it is to be
done. - Stefan wants still to add some
lines, so kindest regards only
and the information that we had
at last a letter from Eva, a
fairly long one. We hope to see her
in February. Best love
Lotte
Dear Hannah and Manfred, we do
not yet know what we shall do in
January. Till now the weather is very
agreeable but if it does not get worse
we shall stay here in our very airy hotel.
As to our voyage to Newyork we have
not yet decided anything. It is at least
13 days voyage, perhaps even more and
rather expensive. Perhaps you could once
ask at the travel-office where we bought
our passage, if we could buy from them
the passage from here to Newyork at the
Mac Coun'd line and they could cable
the passages over here - this would faci-
litate very much our intention and
we are then nearer to England. Should
this be possible please do it and inform
us by cable. We have a lot to do here
with formalities as our permit expires
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, Fortsetzung auf der Rückseite des Aerogramms.

pages.transcription:
soon and to facilitate matters our voyage
in the future we took an unlimited one
which is of cause a sort of garantie not
to depend always on their applications, but
what formalities we has to fulfil, fingerprints
photos with attestations, papers and papers
now it is done and we have never to worry
about delays, difficulties and so on. As to
further lectures I am rather [?] reluctant,
the voyages from country to country in
this enormous continent take days and
days; I prefer to sit quietly and to work
- till now the heat has not yet arrived
and the beauty of this town fascinates
us after weeks more and more. If we
could have you here for a fortnights rest
you would forget all the hard days and
recover physically as morally. Eva got
a very severe letter of us, because she
has not written to us and the same day
finally arrived some scribbled information
from her. I hope she will write now more
regularly to you - we do understand what
her news must mean to you and I wish
I could stand behind her with all my

mental cruelty and force her to write
you twice a week, I can imagine that
even the tiniest and sillest detail of her
is interesting to you. We are here very glad
to have finished with our lectures -
only yesterday I had still one in the
Foreign Office in honour to our friend, the
Cuban minister, whom we lost in an air
accident. Lotte feels allright and I repeat
we should be happy, if we would know you
in safety - I hope you will have both
a few days rest at Bath, at least at
Christmas. We would have liked to send
you some coffee, sugar and similar
Brazilian samples as a Christmas {werend} [?]
but we will ask first, if it is possible
and if there are no special permissions
- one is already screeching formalities
everywhere and I would have liked so
much to show you that we dont forget
you and remember well our last Christ
was in Bath. Let us hope, that our
good and central hours will come again
Yours
Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, Ende des Textes mit Unterschrift.
Farbskala und Grauskala für Archivierung. Darunter ist ein Ausschnitt des Brieftextes (Seite 4) zu sehen.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der kursiven Handschrift. Einzelne Wörter wie 'werend' (evtl. 'present' gemeint) sind aufgrund der Korrektur/Einfügung schwerer zu lesen.
